Electricity and Water Bills Compared Across the GCC

Enter one month's use from your bill and pick who pays to see the same bill at all six utilities, cheapest first.

Prices are in each country's currency and before VAT, except Bahrain (VAT included). Water makes the biggest difference: expats pay KD 2 per 1,000 gallons in Kuwait (about 440 fils per m³), 775 fils per m³ in Bahrain plus 20% wastewater, and AED 7.70–10.41 per m³ in the UAE.

Frequently asked questions

Where are electricity bills cheapest for expats in the GCC?

Kuwait: 5 fils per kWh in investment housing (about 6 UAE fils). A flat using 1,500 kWh and 27 m³ pays about KD 19.4 (AED 231), against about AED 836 in Dubai.

Why are Dubai bills higher than Abu Dhabi or the northern emirates?

DEWA adds a monthly fuel surcharge to electricity and water, and Dubai Municipality bills sewerage per gallon on the DEWA bill, on top of the 5% housing fee on rent (left out of this comparison).

Does the comparison include housing and municipality fees?

No. Rent-based fees are left out because they don't depend on use: Dubai's housing fee and Abu Dhabi's and Bahrain's municipality fees. Each utility's own calculator includes them.

How much less do nationals pay?

For the same use (1,500 kWh and 27 m³): about BD 7 for a Bahraini, KD 7.8 for a Kuwaiti, AED 173 for an Abu Dhabi national, 212 in the northern emirates and 247 in Dubai.
